Small multiples

Source: R/multiples.R
facet_tufte.Rd

Tufte's answer to multivariate data is repetition rather than complication: the same graphic, at the same scale, once per condition, so that comparison is a matter of looking rather than of decoding. Once the reader has learned to read one panel, they have learned to read all of them.

Usage

facet_tufte(facets, ncol = NULL, nrow = NULL, scales = "fixed", ...)

Arguments

facets

Variables to facet by, as with facet_wrap(), for example vars(cyl) or ~ cyl.

ncol, nrow

Panel layout. ncol defaults to NULL, letting ggplot2 choose.

scales

Passed to facet_wrap(). Defaults to "fixed", and warns if you change it, because free scales make panels incomparable.

...

Further arguments passed to facet_wrap().

Value

A ggplot2 facet specification.

Details

This is facet_wrap() with the defaults changed to match that argument. Scales are fixed, because free scales destroy the comparison the design exists to make. Strips are left-aligned and unboxed. The panel count is left to ggplot2 unless you set ncol.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_rangeframe() +
  facet_tufte(~ cyl) +
  theme_tufte()
